input.quote: an assignment, (ii) an exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, fully-paid, freely-assignable license, with the right to sublicense through multiple tiers, or (iii) a non‑exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, fully-paid, freely-assignable license, with the right to sublicense through multiple tiers ((i) through (iii) in order of preference), to PB of any Trial Invention
input.rationale:
This is a co-development/funding agreement, not an inbound licence deal, and no licence is granted to PB by SFJ that could be revoked at will. Instead, PB's IP position is secured by ownership rather than licence: PB is sole and exclusive owner of all Trial Inventions regardless of inventorship (11.1.1.3(a), p0659); SFJ assigns for itself and its Affiliates and must cause its Permitted Third Parties to assign; PB acquires sole and exclusive ownership of the Trial Data Package and Research Results (11.1.1.4, p0663), with a back-up "hereby does assign" on termination together with assignment of all Product Filings (14.3.1–14.3.2, p0783–p0784). Where assignment from SFJ's consultants or Third Party contractors cannot be obtained, the fallback is a worldwide, royalty-free, fully-paid, freely-assignable licence to PB with the right to sublicense through multiple tiers (11.1.1.3(b)–(c), p0660–p0661) — i.e. perpetual, irrevocable in substance, and freely transferable to Affiliates, contractors and successors, which exceeds the preferred position. Section 11.1.1.6 (p0666) runs the other way, limiting SFJ's rights in PB IP, so it benefits us and is not flagged. The only PB-side grants are the SFJ security interest (Art. 7) and the Program Transfer mechanic (3.20), which are outbound and are addressed by other rules. Noted only: PB's use of the Trial Data Package before purchase rests on ownership-transfer mechanics rather than an express interim licence — a drafting nicety, not a fallback failure.</rationale>
